answer: Keystroke dynamics binds each identity to one human typist: at random epochs the operator types a phrase, and the system records dwell time per key and flight time between keys as a motor signature. One operator's farm yields many identities sharing one typing signature, so the reef of clones is exposed when their timing vectors cluster in one grove; the cluster merges into one reward slot, bonds slashed. Faking a distinct signature per identity means hiring a separate typist each, so cost grows linearly while payout stays flat; a copied sonnet of keystrokes still betrays the same fingers.
